thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Possible cross-tenant routing observed in Dedicated pool 'pool-aurorafin-1'. Metric surge + unexpected peer connections to tenant 'aurorafin'. Severity: P2. Please ACK and join #incidents.

sara_eng: ACK. I see the alert graphs in the console, routing anomalies starting ~10:13 UTC. Pulling logs.

liam_sre: I'm oncall. Can someone drop the packet capture command for the node(s)?

ops-bot: Suggested quick checks:
1) `redis-cli -h 10.2.7.4 info` (cache health)
2) `ip route show table 100` on serve-n1
3) `ss -tnp | grep 443` to look for unexpected connections

sara_eng: Running on serve-n1:```bash
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/aurorafin-suspect.pcap host 10.87.12.0/24 and port 443
```Capturing now.

mira_prod: Customer-visible symptoms? AuroraFin engineering says some requests from internal devs returned other customer's model outputs. They flagged PII-like tokens. We need containment and evidence.

liam_sre: Start containment: temp drain the pod group serving aurorafin model variant `aurora-v2-q4_0`. I'm going to cordon the node with the most suspicious routes and evict pods.

sara_eng: Node serve-n1 route table shows:```
# ip route show table 100
10.87.12.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.87.12.9
10.92.0.0/16 via 10.87.12.1 dev eth0 table 100
172.21.0.0/16 via 10.87.12.55 dev eth0
```There's an extra `172.21.0.0/16` route that shouldn't be in this tenant table.

liam_sre: That `172.21` prefix belongs to another customer pool. Looks like a misapplied route. I'm removing it from table 100 now.```bash
sudo ip route del 172.21.0.0/16 table 100 || true
```

ops-bot: Action logged: route-delete invoked by liam_sre at 1951240205. Audit ID: AUD-7591.

sara_eng: tcpdump caught SYNs to 172.21.x.x from the process `redwood-runtime` on PID 2283. Snippet:```
12:14:02.123456 IP 10.87.12.9.55134 > 172.21.9.10.443: Flags [S], seq 0
```

mira_prod: Notifying AuroraFin CSM. Drafting short note: "We've identified a routing misconfiguration in Dedicated pool 'pool-aurorafin-1' that may have caused cross-tenant routing. We're containing traffic and collecting evidence. No confirmed exfil yet; will update in 30m."

liam_sre: Rolling back pods: `kubectl scale deployment/aurora-runtime --replicas=0 -n dedicated-aurorafin` to stop serving while we confirm.

sara_eng: Also capturing KV cache snapshots and KV logs for the time window. Command:```bash
curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_KEY' http://127.0.0.1:9000/debug/kv_dump | gzip -c > /tmp/kv_dump_1951239999.gz
```

dave_sec: Copying evidence to secure bucket (readonly, customer-accessible). We must preserve chain-of-custody. Will create ticket with SR-aurorafin-19512.

liam_sre: After route removal and pod stop, traffic to 172.21.* ceased. Monitoring for stray packets.

sara_eng: Quick sanity checks on other nodes in the same pool show clean tables; this looks like a single-node misconfig during a recent maintenance script run. Searching for the config job: `grep -R "table 100" /etc/maintenance.d/*`

ops-bot: Found maintenance job `apply-tenant-routes.sh` ran at 1951239800 by `deploy-batch` with env var `TARGET_POOL=pool-aurorafin-1`.

mira_prod: Did we have a canary/verification step? If not, we should pause that pipeline. Also need to notify Dedicated operations to block the maintenance run until we audit.

liam_sre: Paging infra infra-pipeline: @deploy-team — please hold `apply-tenant-routes` runs. Evidence suggests race in templating placed a broader prefix into tenant table.

sara_eng: Confirming customer impact: AuroraFin reports ~120 anomalous requests over a 3-minute window. We don't yet have confirmed content overlap, but KV snapshots show potential cache keys that map to a different tenant.

dave_sec: Elevating to security review. Creating incident record in PagerDuty: PD-INC-8273. Notifying Legal for potential PII handling.

mira_prod: For customer comms: proposed message for AuroraFin support (short):
"We detected a routing misconfiguration in your Dedicated pool that could have routed a small number of requests to an incorrect tenant cache. We've contained the issue, removed the route, collected logs/pcaps, and will share a forensics packet within 48 hours. No confirmed exfiltration at this time."

liam_sre: Next steps checklist:
- [x] Remove rogue route on serve-n1
- [x] Stop aurora runtime pods on affected nodes
- [x] Capture pcaps & KV dumps (done)
- [ ] Full audit of maintenance jobs/templates for templating bug
- [ ] Forensic review of captured content by security
- [ ] Postmortem + prevention plan

sara_eng: Evidence artifacts:
- `/tmp/aurorafin-suspect.pcap` (sha256: abcd1234...)
- `/tmp/kv_dump_1951239999.gz` (sha256: ef56...)
- Audit log `AUD-7591` and maintenance run `apply-tenant-routes@1951239800`

ops-bot: Noted customer SLA implications. Recommend offering AuroraFin priority root-cause timeline and a dedicated support call.

mira_prod: Scheduling exec sync with AuroraFin in 60 minutes. Will include Security + SRE.

dave_sec: Quick mitigation suggestion to prevent recurrence: add strict ip route validation in maintenance job: verify doesn't insert prefixes outside allocated tenant CIDR list. I'll work with infra to add checks.

liam_sre: Leaving steps for follow-up post-incident: validate no other pools have stray entries, add unit test in route templating, and instrument route-change alerts.

sara_eng: Closing the immediate page — system stabilized at 12:28 UTC. Moving to follow-up channel #incidents-postmortems for root-cause and action items.

ops-bot: Incident state updated: mitigated -> containment. Transitioning to follow-up. PD-INC-8273 set to 'investigating' -> 'mitigated' at 1951240500.

liam_sre: Thanks team. I'll produce a short timeline and upload the artifacts to the secure case folder by EOD.

mira_prod: I'll coordinate customer updates and the support call.

sara_eng: Ping me for any missing logs.

oncall-bot: Reminder: postmortem template -> https://intranet.redwood/postmortems. Please include incident ID PD-INC-8273 and the audit IDs.
